meaning.de:
Das Zeichen besteht aus sechs ungeteilten Strichen. Die ungeteilten Striche entsprechen der lichten, starken, geistigen, tätigen Urkraft. Das Zeichen ist ganz einheitlich stark in seiner Natur. Da ihm keinerlei Schwäche anhaftet, ist es seiner Eigenschaft nach die Kraft. Sein Bild ist der Himmel. Die Kraft wird dargestellt als nicht gebunden an bestimmte räumliche Verhältnisse. Darum wird sie aufgefaßt als Bewegung. Als Grundlage dieser Bewegung kommt die Zeit in Betracht. So ist denn auch die Macht der Zeit und die Macht des Beharrens in der Zeit, die Dauer, in dem Zeichen begriffen.

Bei der Erklärung des Zeichens ist durchgehend eine doppelte Deutung zu berücksichtigen: die makrokosmische und die Wirkung in der Menschenwelt. Auf das Weltgeschehen angewandt ist in dem Zeichen das starke schöpferische Wirken der Gottheit ausgedrückt. Auf die Menschenwelt angewandt bezeichnet es das schöpferische Wirken der heiligen und weisen Person, des Herrschers und Führers der Menschen, der ihr höheres Wesen durch seine Kraft weckt und entwickelt . (Das Zeichen ist dem 4- Monat (Mai-Juni) zugeordnet, wenn die lichte Kraft auf ihrer Höhe steht, noch ehe die Sonnenwende den Rückgang des Jahres beginnt.)
meaning.en:
The hexagram consists of six undivided lines. The undivided lines correspond to the light, strong, spiritual, active primal power. The hexagram is uniformly strong in its nature throughout. Since no weakness clings to it, its essential attribute is strength. Its image is heaven. Strength is here represented as not bound to any specific spatial conditions. It is therefore conceived as movement. Time is regarded as the basis of this movement. Thus the hexagram includes both the power of time and the power of perseverance in time, that is, duration.
In interpreting the hexagram, a twofold meaning must everywhere be considered: the macrocosmic, and the working in the world of human beings. Applied to cosmic events, the hexagram expresses the strong creative working of the deity. Applied to the human world, it denotes the creative action of the holy and wise person, of the ruler and leader of humankind, who through his power awakens and develops their higher nature. (The hexagram is assigned to the fourth month [May–June], when the light power stands at its height, before the solstice begins the year's decline.)

line7.interpretation.en: If one wishes to climb so high that one loses touch with the rest of humankind, one becomes isolated, and this necessarily leads to failure. Here lies a warning against a titanic striving upward that exceeds one's strength. A fall into the depths would be the consequence.

meaning.en:
The hexagram consists entirely of divided lines. The divided line corresponds to the shadowy, soft, receptive primal power of yin. The attribute of the hexagram is devotion; its image is the earth. It is the perfect counterpart of the Creative — the counterpart, not the opposite; a complement, not a combatant. It is nature as against spirit, earth as against heaven, space as against time, the womanly-maternal as against the manly-paternal. The principle of this counterpart, transferred to human conditions, is found, however, not only in the relations between man and woman, but also between prince and minister or father and son; indeed, in the individual person themselves this duality is present as the coexistence of the spiritual and the sensuous.
Yet one cannot speak of a real dualism, for between the two hexagrams there is the relation of a clear order of rank. In itself, of course, the Receptive is just as important as the Creative. But the attribute of devotion defines the position of this primal power in relation to the Creative. It must stand under the guidance and stimulation of the Creative; only then does it work salutary effect. Only when it steps out of this position and seeks to set itself beside the Creative as an equal does it become evil. Out of this then arises opposition and struggle against the Creative, which proves disastrous for both parties.

All beings have need of nourishment from above. But the giving of food has its time, which one must await. The hexagram shows the clouds in the heavens that give rain to gladden all that grows and to provide people with food and drink. This rain will come in its time. One cannot force it; one must wait for it. The thought of waiting is further suggested by the attributes of the two primary trigrams: within, strength; before it, danger. Strength in the face of danger does not overhurl itself, but is able to wait, while weakness in the face of danger is thrown into agitation and lacks the patience to wait.

The image of the upper primary trigram, Ch'ien, is heaven; that of the lower, Li, is flame. The nature of fire is to flame upward toward heaven. This gives the idea of fellowship. The second line is the one that, through its central nature, unites the five strong lines around itself. The sign is the counterpart of No. 7, The Army. There: danger within, obedience without, as the nature of the warlike army, which for its cohesion requires the one strong among the many weak. Here: clarity within, strength without, as the nature of the peaceful union of human beings, which for its cohesion requires the one yielding among the many firm.

line2.interpretation.en: Here lies the danger of a special party on the basis of personal and selfish interests. Such factions, which are exclusive and have no room for all, which must condemn a part of humankind in order to gather the rest, arise from low motives and therefore lead, in the long run, to humiliation.

line6.interpretation.en: Here the warm bond of the heart is missing. One stands, in fact, already outside the fellowship with others. Yet one joins on. The fellowship does not embrace all, but only those who dwell outwardly together. The meadow is the pasture before the city. The ultimate goal of the union of humankind is here not yet reached. Yet one need make no reproach to oneself. One joins society without special purposes.

meaning.en: The fire in the heaven above shines far, so that all things come into the light and into appearance. The weak fifth line is in the place of honor, and all the strong lines correspond to it. Those who, in a high place, are modest and gentle, have everything fall to them. (The meaning of the sign agrees with the word of Jesus: Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth.).

The sign is composed of Ken, Keeping Still, the mountain, and K'un. The mountain is the youngest son of the Creative, the representative of heaven on earth. He dispenses downward the blessings of heaven, clouds and rain, that gather about his summit, and thereupon shines forth transfigured in heavenly light. This shows modesty and its effect in high and strong human beings. Above stands K'un, the earth. The quality of the earth is lowliness, but for this very reason it is presented in this sign as exalted, in that it is above, over the mountain. This shows the effect of modesty in lowly, simple human beings: they are thereby exalted.

Above is Kien, Heaven; below is Dschen, movement. The lower trigram, Dschen, is determined by the strong line that it has received from above, from Heaven. When movement accordingly follows the law of Heaven, then the human being is innocent and without guile. This is the genuine, the natural, untroubled by any calculation or ulterior motive. Where intention becomes apparent, there the truth and innocence of nature are lost. Nature without the directive of the spirit is not true nature, but degenerate nature. From the idea of the natural, the formation of thought proceeds in part still further, and so the hexagram also embraces the idea of the unintended, the unexpected.

meaning.de: Das »Schöpferische« wird durch das »Stillehalten« bezähmt. Das gibt eine große Kraft, ganz anders als bei Nr. 9, wo nur das »Sanfte« das »Schöpferische« bezähmt. Während dort ein schwacher Strich die fünf Starken bezähmen soll, sind es hier zwei, außer dem Minister auch noch der Fürst. Darum ist ihre Zähmungskraft weit stärker. Eine dreifache Bedeutung liegt in dem Zeichen: der Himmel inmitten des Bergs gibt den Gedanken des Festhaltens = Beisammenhaltens; das Zeichen Gen, welches das Zeichen Kien stillhält, gibt den Gedanken des Festhaltens = Zurückhaltens. Indem schließlich ein starker Strich oben der Herr des Zeichens ist, der als weise Person geehrt und gepflegt wird, so ergibt sich hieraus der Gedanke des Festhaltens = Pflege, Ernährung. Der letzte Gedanke kommt namentlich bei dem Herrn des Zeichens, dem starken oberen Strich, der die weise Person repräsentiert, zur Geltung.

meaning.en: The hexagram consists of the doubling of the trigram K'an. It is one of the eight double hexagrams. The trigram K'an means a plunging in. A yang line has plunged in between two yin lines and is enclosed by them, like water in a ravine. It is the middle son. The Receptive has attained the middle line of the Creative, and thus K'an arises. As image it is water—the water that comes from above and is in motion on earth in rivers and streams, and that brings about all life on earth. Transferred to the human being, it represents the heart, the soul enclosed in the body, the light contained in the dark, reason. The name of the hexagram, because it is doubled, bears the addition: Repetition of Danger. By this the hexagram is to designate an objective situation to which one must accustom oneself, not a subjective disposition. For danger as a subjective disposition means either foolhardiness or guile. Therefore danger is also designated as a ravine, that is, a condition in which one finds oneself like the water in a ravine, and out of which one comes as does the water, by behaving rightly.

meaning.de: Die Sonne ist hier unter die Erde gesunken, daher verdunkelt. Der Name des Zeichens bedeutet eigentlich Verwundung des Hellen, daher die einzelnen Linien auch vielfach von Verwundungen reden. Die Situation ist genau die entgegengesetzte wie beim vorigen Zeichen. Dort eine weise Person an der Spitze, die tüchtige Gehilfen hat, mit denen sie gemeinsam voranschreitet; hier eine finstere Person an maßgebender Stelle, durch die die tüchtige und weise Person geschädigt wird.
meaning.en: The sun has here sunk beneath the earth and is therefore darkened. The name of the hexagram actually means the wounding of the bright, and for this reason the individual lines also speak in many places of woundings. The situation is exactly the reverse of that in the previous hexagram. There, a wise person at the top who has capable assistants with whom they advance together; here, a dark person in the authoritative position, by whom the capable and wise are harmed.

judgment.en:
The Family. The perseverance of the woman furthers.
The foundation of the family rests on the relations of husband and wife. The bond that holds the family together lies in the fidelity and perseverance of the wife. Her place is within (the second line), the place of the man is without (the fifth line). That man and woman take their proper places corresponds to the great laws of nature. In the family firm authority is needed: these are the parents. When the father is truly father and the son son, when the elder brother fills his place as elder brother and the younger his place as younger brother, when the husband is truly husband and the wife wife, then the family is in order. When the family is in order, then the whole of the social relations of humankind come into order. Of the five social relations, three lie within the family: that between father and son — love; between husband and wife — discipline; between elder and younger brother — order. The loving reverence of the son is then further transferred to the prince as loyalty of duty, and the order and affection of the brothers to the friend as fidelity, and the relation to superiors as subordination. The family is the germ-cell of society, the natural soil on which the practice of the moral duties is facilitated by natural affection, so that in the narrow circle the foundation is created from which they are then transferred to human relations in general.

line2.interpretation.en: True increase comes through creating in oneself the conditions for it: receptivity and love of the good. Thereby what is striven for comes of itself with the necessity of a law of nature. Where increase is thus in accord with the highest laws of the world, it cannot be hindered by any constellation of chance. Everything depends only on not allowing oneself to be made frivolous by unexpected good fortune, but on making it one's own through inner strength and steadfastness. Then one gains significance before God and before people and can effect something for the good of the world.

meaning.en: Above is the lake, the water beneath it. The lake is empty and exhausted. In yet another way the thought of exhaustion comes forth: above a dark line that holds down two light ones below; below a light line is wedged in between two dark ones. The upper trigram belongs to the dark principle, while the lower belongs to the light principle. Thus everywhere the noble ones are oppressed and held within bounds by the common ones.

line5.interpretation.en: It is someone who has at heart the welfare of all, oppressed from above and below (this is the meaning of the severed nose and feet). One finds no help from those whose duty it would be to assist in the work of deliverance (the ministers wore purple knee-bands). Yet things gradually develop for the better. Until then it is important, in strong inner gathering, to step before God and to pray and sacrifice for the welfare of the whole.

meaning.de:
Das ganze Zeichen ist das Bild des Tiegels, unten die Beine, dann der Bauch, dann die Ohren, bzw. Henkel, und oben die Ringe zum Tragen. Das Bild des Tiegels legt gleichzeitig den Gedanken der Ernährung nahe. Der Tiegel, aus Bronze gegossen, war das Gerät, das im Ahnentempel und bei Festmählern die gekochten Speisen enthielt. Aus ihm wurden sie vom Hausherrn in die Schüssel der Gäste geschöpft.

Auch der Brunnen hat den Nebengedanken der Nahrungsspende aber mehr für das Volk. Der Tiegel als Gerät der verfeinerten Kultur legt Pflege und Ernährung der tüchtigen Menschen nahe deren Pflege der Staatsregierung zugute kam (vgl. die vier Zeichen der Ernährung, Nr. 5, 27, 48, 50).

Dieses Zeichen und das Zeichen »Brunnen« sind die beiden einzigen Zeichen im Buch der Wandlungen, die konkrete künstliche Gegenstände darstellen. Allein auch hier hat der Gedanke seine abstrakte Seite. Unten Sun ist Holz und Wind, oben Li ist die Flamme; es stellt also die durch Holz und Wind entfachte Flamme dar, die ebenfalls den Gedanken der Speisenbereitung nahelegt.
meaning.en:
The whole hexagram is the image of the caldron: below the legs, then the belly, then the ears or handles, and above the rings for carrying. The image of the caldron likewise suggests the thought of nourishment. The caldron, cast in bronze, was the vessel that in the temple of the ancestors and at festive banquets held the cooked viands. From it they were ladled by the master of the house into the dishes of the guests.
The well too has the secondary thought of providing nourishment, but more for the people. The caldron as a vessel of refined culture suggests the cultivation and nourishment of able people, whose cultivation came to the benefit of the government of the state (compare the four hexagrams of nourishment, Nos. 5, 27, 48, 50).
This hexagram and the hexagram "The Well" are the only two in the Book of Changes that represent concrete man-made objects. Yet here too the thought has its abstract side. Below, Sun is wood and wind; above, Li is the flame; thus it represents the flame kindled by wood and wind, which likewise suggests the thought of preparing food.

The image of the hexagram is the mountain, the youngest son of heaven and earth. The masculine is above, where by its nature it strives, the feminine below, where the direction of its movement leads. Thus stillness is at hand, since movement has reached its normal end.
Applied to the human being, the problem shown is that of attaining the stillness of the heart. The heart is very hard to bring to rest. Whereas Buddhism strives for rest through the dying away of all movement in Nirvana, the standpoint of the Book of Changes is that rest is only a polar state which has movement as its complement throughout.
Perhaps in the words of the text instructions for yoga practice are contained.

meaning.de:
Der See hat einen beschränkten Raum. Wenn mehr Wasser hineinkommt, so fließt er über. Darum muß man ihm Schranken setzen. Es sind im Bild die Wasser unten und die Wasser oben, zwischen denen die Feste des Himmels als Schranke ist.

Das chinesische Wort für Beschränkung bedeutet eigentlich die festen Glieder, durch die die Bambusstengel eingeteilt sind. Im gewöhnlichen Leben ist damit gemeint die Sparsamkeit, die feste Schranken für ihre Ausgaben hat. Im moralischen Leben sind es die festen Schranken, die sich die edle Person steckt für ihre Handlungen, die Schranken der Treue und der Uneigennützigkeit.
meaning.en:
The lake has a limited space. When more water comes into it, it overflows. Therefore limits must be set for it. In the image are the waters below and the waters above, between which the firmament of heaven serves as a limit.
The Chinese word for limitation properly means the firm joints by which the bamboo stalks are divided. In ordinary life it denotes the thrift that sets firm limits on expenditures. In the moral life it denotes the firm limits the noble one sets for their actions — the limits of fidelity and unselfishness.
